messages:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in GPU attach failures in north1c. ~15% of LLM pods fail with attach timeout + metadata fetch errors. Also seeing packet loss to 169.254.x.y from that AZ.

sre-bot: Alert: GPU_ATTACH_FAILURE_RATE > 10% (north1c) for 5m. Avg attach latency 3.2s, error 504 on metadata fetch. Incident ID #INC-2069.

trent: Copy. Can someone confirm scope — is this only GPU attach or broader network flakiness for north1c? Any per-tenant impact metrics? @oncall

lei: Looks like it's starting at the node level — kubelet logs show repeated `attach disk` timeouts and `failed to fetch metadata` on node bootstrap. I suspect a localized NIC firmware issue or a switch with high error rate. Tenant impact: serving p95 latency up 80ms for jobs scheduled into north1c; failing requests are being retried and hitting other AZs.

ops-jordan: I'll start a targeted cordon/drain on the worst nodes and shift LB weights for north1c to 20% to limit new placements. Commands I'll use:
```
kubectl get nodes -l topology.kubernetes.io/zone=north1c -o wide
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=10m
```

sam: FYI on cost — draining will force pods to other AZs and may trigger burst to dedicated pools. Expect short-term CPU/GPU overcommit and some spot preemptions. We should prefer warm reserved nodes in north1a/b to absorb traffic before scaling large.

trent: Agreed. Plan: 1) cordon/gradual-drain 2) shift LB weights north1c -> 20% 3) spin warm nodes in north1a/1b (reserved pools) 4) temporarily disable aggressive binpacking autoscaler for serving to avoid mass consolidation 5) monitor cache warm and latency. Who's taking node drains?

ops-jordan: Taking it. Starting drains now. Draining in 10% batches to avoid mass KV cache invalidation.

maya: I'm updating the incident doc and notifying EU/NA customers that may hit higher latency. Putting canary fallback model route to smaller model when retries spike.

ops-jordan: Status: drained 6/24 nodes in north1c; attach error rate down to 9% from 15%. LB north1c weight -> 35% (gradual).

lei: Good. Also make sure we set `--max-surge` low on any deployments to avoid concurrent restarts. And keep KV cache warm by pinning high-traffic prefixes into north1a for the moment.

sam: Started 12 reserved GPUs in north1a and 8 in north1b; scaled down spot pools to reduce preemption risk. Cost hit minimal compared to potential SLA breaches.

trent: Can we get network team to check north1c top-of-rack and switch error counters? @netops

maya: Netops acknowledged, running diagnostics. They see elevated CRC/tx-error on two leafs, will open cloud provider ticket for NIC firmware rollback as a precaution.

ops-jordan: Status update: LB weight north1c -> 30%, draining 12/24. Errors now 5%. No new attach failures in last 2m for drained nodes.

lei: If errors hold, leave cordon on remaining nodes and don't uncordon until provider confirms fix. We'll continue staggered uncordon after 1h stabilization test.

maya: Agreed. I'll keep cordon and monitoring. Adding runbook snippet to incident:
```
# Immediate steps
1. Cordon worst nodes in AZ
2. Drain in small batches: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
3. Shift LB weights: scale back new placements to 20-35% for affected AZ
4. Warm reserved instances in healthy AZs
5. Disable aggressive binpack autoscaling during drain
6. Engage netops and provider support
```

ops-jordan: Final-ish: drained 18/24 nodes; attach errors down to baseline 1.2%. Netops created provider ticket CLD-9876 for NIC fw rollback. Keeping cordon on remaining nodes for 1h.

sam: Noted. I'll file cost ack to finance for the temporary reserved capacity bump.

trent: Thanks team. I'll keep the incident open for the 1h verification window. If stable, we'll uncordon gradually. Great job. :thumbsup:
